Hi Lisa —

Appreciate the RFI. I've pulled together an initial intake workbook (redwood_initial_intake.xlsx) and a data-pathways diagram that maps our hosted, dedicated, and private offerings to typical PHI flows. High-level answers below and next steps:

Quick answers:
- PHI flows: Hosted API (hosted) keeps customer data encrypted in a shared control plane; Private (VPC/on-prem) isolates control plane and allows in-region compute. The attached diagram highlights where PHI may persist (logs, KV caches, backups).
- Retention: Per-customer retention controls are supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted has configurable retention windows and data deletion APIs.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments; hosted supports our managed keys with dedicated key scoping for enterprise tiers.
- BAA scope: We can include storage, backups, logs, and limited telemetry. Subprocessor disclosure is standard; we provide a subprocessors list and update cadence.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a draft BAA by EOD Monday (drive link below).
2) We can schedule a 30-minute technical Q&A (security + infra) early next week to walk through the diagram and clarify retention options.
3) If needed, our Solutions Architect can produce a short data residency statement for your legal team.

Can you confirm whether Bridger requires US-only residency and whether the procurement deadline Oct 8 is firm?

Best,

Lisa —

Attached is our initial BAA draft (redwood_draft_BAA_v1.docx) and a retention matrix in the intake workbook. Summary of the retention defaults and options:

- Logs: Default 90 days; configurable down to 0 for Dedicated/Private with documented deletion procedures.
- Transcript caches (KV/prefix cache): Default 7 days; can be disabled or scoped per-tenant on Dedicated/Private.
- Backups: System snapshots are weekly by default and retained 30 days; per-tenant snapshotting is available only on Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Backups encryption: All backups are encrypted at rest; Private supports customer KMS.

Action items:
- Marissa: can you review the BAA draft and flag anything Jordan should look at from a legal perspective?
- Jordan: please review the subprocessors clause; Bridger has an explicit requirement for advance notice 30 days prior to new subprocessors.
- Lisa: confirm whether Bridger will accept BAA redlines on your standard template or if you require Redwood's form.

I'll be on the technical Q&A on Tue 09/29 10am PT — calendar invite sent.

Thanks,
